'''uvulatome''' (ū′vū-lạ-tōm), ''n.'' [< L. ''uvula'', uvula, + Gr. -τομος, < τέμνειν, ταμεῖν, cut.] An instrument for cutting off the lower part of the uvula.

'''uwarowite,''' ''n.'' Same as ''uvarovite.''

'''uxorial''' (uk-sō′ri-al), ''a.'' [< L. ''uxor'', a wife, + ''-i-al.''] '''1.''' Of or pertaining to a wife or married woman; peculiar to or befitting a wife.
{{smaller block|Favorinus . . . calls this said stata forma the beauty of wives, the ''uxorial'' beauty. {{right|''Bulwer'', My Novel, iv.}}}}
'''2.''' Same as ''uxorious.''
{{smaller block|Riccabocca . . . melted into absolute ''uxorial'' imbecility at the sight of that mute distress.
{{right|''Bulwer'', My Novel, viii. 12.}}}}
[Rare in both uses.]

'''uxoricidal''' (uk-sō′ri-sī-dạl), ''a.'' [< ''uxoricide''<sup>2</sup> + ''-al.''] Of or pertaining to uxoricide; tending to uxoricide. ''Cornhill Mag.''

'''uxoricide<sup>1</sup>''' (uk-sō′ri-sīd), ''n.'' [< L. ''uxor'', a wife, + ''-cida'', < ''cædere'', kill.] One who slays his wife.

'''uxoricide<sup>2</sup>''' (uk-sō′ri-sīd), ''n.'' [< L. ''uxor'', a wife, + ''-cidium'', < ''cædere'', slay.] The killing of a wife by her husband.

'''uxorious''' (uk-sō′ri-us), ''a.'' [< L. ''uxorius'', of or pertaining to a wife, < ''uxor'', a wife.] Excessively or foolishly fond of a wife; doting on a wife.
{{smaller block|Towards his queen he was nothing ''uxorious'', nor scarce indulgent. {{right|''Bacon'', Hist. Henry VII.}}}}
readings.c3s3:
¶
'''uxoriously''' (uk-sō′ri-us-li), ''adv.'' In an uxorious manner; with foolish or doting fondness for a wife.
{{smaller block|<poem>If thou art thus ''uxoriously'' inclin’d
To bear thy bondage with a willing mind,
Prepare thy neck. ''Dryden'', tr. of Juvenal, vi. 292.</poem>}}

'''uxoriousness''' (uk-sō′ri-us-nes), ''n.'' The state or character of being uxorious; connubial dotage; foolish fondness for a wife.

'''Uzbeg, Usbeg''' (uz′-, us′beg), ''n.'' [Tatar.] A member of a Turkish race, of mixed origin, resident in central Asia.

'''uzzard''' (uz′ärd), ''n.'' A dialectal form of ''izzard''<sup>1</sup>. ''Halliwell.''

'''uzzle''' (uz′l), ''n.'' A dialectal form of ''ouzel.''

A small free conical body, projecting downward and backward from the middle of the pendulous margin of the soft palate, composed of the uvular muscles covered by mucous membrane. See cuts under ''tonsil'' and ''mouth.''—'''2.''' A prominent section of the inferior vermiform process of the cerebellum, in advance of the pyramid, between the two lateral lobes known as the ''amygdalæ'' or ''tonsils'': so called from being likened to the uvula of the palate.—'''3.''' A slight projection of mucous membrane from the bladder into the cystic orifice of the urethra; the uvula vesicæ, luette vésicale, or uvula of the bladder.—{{smaller|'''Azygos uvulæ.'''
